requirement_text.REQ-428: Third MOB-4 requirement. Task routes (lib/letflow/routers/tasks.ex): GET /api/v1/tasks/inbox, GET /api/v1/tasks/:id, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/claim, POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete. The task form is resolved through REQ-424's pinned resolver and rendered by REQ-427's form renderer; never the active version. Process-instance renderer: read-only view of GET /api/v1/instances/:id and /api/v1/instances/:id/timeline (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex) -- status, current step, timeline. No cancel/rebind/advance actions (not in MOB-4). All screens use REQ-426's six-state wrapper; claim/complete errors (409 already claimed, 403, 422) map to its states.

task.description: This is a mobile-only run (apps/mobile/ only, no lib/letflow/ or web/ change) -- per WF-02 Step 3's own scope note, Dart tests under apps/mobile/test/ are written by MOBILE-DEV in the mobile step, same as the REQ-425/427 precedent (see handoffs/WF02-REQ425-20260929/step-03-test-designer.json for the established pattern: TEST-DESIGNER independently verifies MOBILE-DEV's existing Dart tests against each decomposed acceptance criterion rather than writing new Dart test files from scratch). Apply the ISS-0880 lesson explicitly: decompose EVERY multi-clause acceptance criterion into its individual clauses and confirm each clause has its own test that would fail if that specific clause were violated -- not one test covering the AC's gestalt. In particular AC1 has at least 4 sub-clauses (list inbox / claim / open / complete-with-form-values-in-body) and AC4 has at least 3 (status rendered / timeline entries rendered / no cancel-rebind-advance action exposed) -- each needs its own traceable test, named explicitly in your spec. Read the actual test files in artifacts_in (not MOBILE-DEV's handoff summary) and verify genuine coverage; write any missing test yourself if a real gap is found (do not rubber-stamp). Write test/specs/REQ-428.md documenting the full clause-by-clause mapping. Re-run, from apps/mobile/: flutter analyze && flutter test yourself and quote the real output.
acceptance_criteria: a test lists the inbox from a fake GET /api/v1/tasks/inbox, claims a task (asserting POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/claim), opens it, and completes it (asserting POST /api/v1/tasks/:id/complete with the form values in the body)
a test asserts opening a task pinned to form_version 1 while version 2 is cached renders version 1's fields (through REQ-424's resolver), not version 2's
a test asserts a 409 on claim renders a state telling the user the task is no longer available and refreshes the inbox, not a crash
a test asserts the process-instance screen renders status and timeline entries from fake /instances/:id and /instances/:id/timeline responses and exposes no cancel, rebind or advance action
`cd apps/mobile && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass, real output quoted
